timeline.label: First filing-grounded Marvin deep dive; contract base value $412.52/sh vs ~$352 price (+2.3% seven-year synthesis)
Q2 2026: operating revenue $14.8B (NII $4.6B + non-interest income $10.2B); cash $45.2B, debt $57.0B
FY2025: revenue net of interest expense $72.2B, net income $10.83B, EPS $15.38; owner earnings normalized $16.0B
FY2025 cash from operations $18.4B and capital spending $2.4B anchor normalized owner earnings reinvestment model
FY2024 revenue net of interest expense $65.9B and net income $10.13B; continued post-pandemic spending recovery
Accelerated investment in card member acquisition and digital capabilities after pandemic trough in travel and entertainment spend
COVID-19 shock to travel and entertainment billed business; credit reserves elevated then released as spend recovered
Expanded merchant acceptance and partnership model versus pure proprietary closed-loop historical footprint
Global financial crisis stressed funding and credit; TARP-era support and subsequent balance sheet repair
Founded as express mail and travel services; evolved into global payments and card lending franchise

industry.structure: Global card payments oligopoly: closed-loop issuers (American Express) compete with open-network schemes (Visa, Mastercard) and bank issuers for affluent spenders and merchant acceptance.
industry.share_shift: American Express gains share when premium card member spending and merchant discount revenue grow faster than industry; bank co-brand and fintech rewards programs pressure acquisition economics.
industry.trend: Higher interest rates supported net interest income on card loans while fee income scales with billed business; normalization of credit and funding spreads is the key swing factor.

top_claims.claim: At $351.93 (Yahoo close 2026-07-20), our base case annual return is 2.3% per year over seven years on proof-backed economic value of $412.52 per share. American Express is a global payments compounder with a narrow moat from its closed-loop network and premium brand. FY2025 normalized owner earnings were $16.0 billion
*Primary risk: Credit losses and funding costs rise together in a recession, compressing returns on the card receivable book while rewards spending stays elevated to retain card members.
Consumer credit deterioration could force reserve builds beyond current provision levels (`10-K_20260206`, credit quality discussion).

risk_claims.claim: *Primary risk: Credit losses and funding costs rise together in a recession, compressing returns on the card receivable book while rewards spending stays elevated to retain card members.
Consumer credit deterioration could force reserve builds beyond current provision levels (`10-K_20260206`, credit quality discussion).
Funding spread compression: wholesale and deposit costs may outrun card lending yields if rates fall unevenly (`10-Q_20260724`, net interest income).
